readings.title: The Ignition of Elihu's Zeal
readings.subtitle: Elihu’s spirit is provoked by Iyoḇ's self-righteousness and the elders' failure to defend Elohim's justice.
readings.text:
[Job 32:1] Then these three men ceased to answer Iyoḇ, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
[2] And the wrath of Elihu, son of Baraḵ’ěl the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, burned against Iyoḇ. His wrath burned because he declared himself right rather than <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[3] And against his three friends his wrath burned, because they had found no answer, and pronounced <dn>Elohim</dn> wrong.
[4] And because they were years older than he, Elihu had waited to speak to Iyoḇ.
[5] And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath burned.

readings.title: The Source of True Understanding
readings.subtitle: Elihu declares that the breath of the Almighty, not mere accumulation of days, grants wisdom to mortal man.
readings.text:
[Job 32:6] And Elihu, son of Baraḵ’ěl the Buzite, responded and said, “I am young in years, and you are aged. Therefore I was afraid to let you know my opinion.
[7] I said, ‘Days should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.’
[8] But truly it is the spirit in man and the breath of the <dn>Almighty</dn> that gives him understanding.
[9] The multitude are not wise, nor do the aged understand right-ruling.
[10] Therefore I have said, ‘Listen to me, let me also make <dn>את</dn> my opinion known to you.’

readings.title: The Futility of Mortal Arguments
readings.subtitle: Observing the elders' defeat, Elihu resolves to present a defense grounded in the Creator’s authority.
readings.text:
[Job 32:11] Look, I waited for your words, I listened to your reasonings, while you searched out what to say.
[12] And I paid close attention to you. But look, not one of you proved Iyoḇ wrong, nor answered his words.
[13] Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom’ – it is <dn>Ěl</dn> that drives him away, not man.
[14] Now he has not ordered words against me, so I would not answer him with your words.

readings.title: The Silence of the Elders
readings.subtitle: The collapse of retributive arguments leaves a void that must be filled by truth.
readings.text:
[Job 32:15] They have broken down; they have not answered again; words have departed from them.
[16] And I have waited, but they do not speak, because they have stood still, they answered no more.
[17] Let me answer on my part, let me also make my opinion known.

readings.title: Pressed by the Ruach
readings.subtitle: Compelled by internal spiritual pressure, Elihu speaks without partiality out of reverence for his Maker.
readings.text:
[Job 32:18] For I am filled with words; the spirit within me presses me.
[19] See, within me it is like wine not opened; it shall burst like new wineskins.
[20] Let me speak, so that I find relief; let me open my lips and answer.
[21] Please, let me not show partiality to anyone, nor let me flatter any man.
[22] For I do not know how to flatter, lest my <dn>Maker</dn> should soon take me away!

readings.title: An Equal Before Ěl
readings.subtitle: Elihu approaches Iyoḇ not with crushing superiority, but as a fellow vessel formed from the same clay.
readings.text:
[Job 33:1] “And yet, O Iyoḇ, please hear my speech and listen to all my words.
[2] See, please! I shall open my mouth, my tongue shall speak in my mouth.
[3] My words are from the uprightness of my heart, my lips shall speak knowledge clearly.
[4] The Spirit of <dn>Ěl</dn> has made me, and the breath of the <dn>Almighty</dn> gives me life.
[5] If you are able, answer me, set yourself in order before me, take your stand.
[6] See, I am like you before <dn>Ěl</dn>, I too have been formed out of clay.
[7] See, no fear of me should alarm you, nor should pressure by me be heavy on you.

readings.title: Challenging the Claim of Flawlessness
readings.subtitle: Iyoḇ’s assertion of absolute innocence and his accusation of divine hostility are met with the absolute truth: Eloah is greater than man.
readings.text:
[Job 33:8] But you have spoken in my hearing, and the sound of words I hear, saying,
[9] I am clear, without transgression; I am innocent, and I have no crookedness.
[10] See, <dn>He</dn> finds occasions against me, <dn>He</dn> counts me as <dn>His</dn> enemy;
[11] <dn>He</dn> puts my feet in the stocks, <dn>He</dn> watches all my paths.’
[12] See, in this you have not been righteous. Let me answer you: <dn>Eloah</dn> is greater than man!
[13] Why have you complained against <dn>Him</dn>? Because <dn>He</dn> does not answer all <dn>His</dn> matters?

readings.title: The Providential Wake-Up Call
readings.subtitle: The Almighty communicates through night visions and the crucible of physical distress to deter man's life from the pit.
readings.text:
[Job 33:14] For <dn>Ěl</dn> does speak once, or twice – though one does not notice it –
[15] in a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men, while slumbering on a bed,
[16] then <dn>He</dn> opens the ears of men, and seals <dn>את</dn> their instruction,
[17] to turn man from his deed, and conceal pride from man.
[18] <dn>He</dn> keeps back his being from the pit, and his life from passing away by the sword.
[19] And he is reproved with pain on his bed, and with unceasing distress in his bones,
[20] so that his life loathes bread, and his being desirable food.
[21] His flesh wastes away, and his bones which were not seen stick out.
[22] And his being draws near the pit, and his life to the destroyers.

readings.title: The Restorative Atonement
readings.subtitle: A chosen mediator reveals the path of straightness, releasing the repentant soul to experience premial justice and fresh life.
readings.text:
[Job 33:23] If there is a messenger for him, a mediator, one among a thousand, to show man <dn>His</dn> straightness,
[24] then <dn>He</dn> shows favour to him, and says, ‘Release him from going down to the pit, <dn>I</dn> have found an atonement.
[25] Let his flesh become fresher than a child’s, let him return to the days of his youth.’
[26] He prays to <dn>Eloah</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> accepts him. And he sees <dn>His</dn> face with joy, and <dn>He</dn> restores to man his righteousness.
[27] He sings to men and says, ‘I have sinned, and I have perverted <dn>את</dn> what was right, and it did not profit me.
[28] <dn>He</dn> has redeemed <dn>את</dn> my being from going down to the pit, and my life sees the light.’

readings.title: The Light of the Living
readings.subtitle: Ěl orchestrates these cycles of testing and redemption to continually draw adam-kind back from destruction.
readings.text:
[Job 33:29] See, <dn>Ěl</dn> does all these – twice, three times with a man,
[30] to bring back his being from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
[31] Pay attention, Iyoḇ, listen to me, keep silent, and let me speak.
[32] If there are words, answer me; speak, for I desire to declare you right.
[33] If not, listen to me, keep silent, and let me teach you wisdom.”

readings.title: The Call for Discernment
readings.subtitle: Elihu summons the wise to weigh Iyoḇ’s dangerous conclusion that delighting in Elohim yields no profit.
readings.text:
[Job 34:1] Then Elihu responded and said,
[2] “Hear my words, you wise men; give ear to me, you who have knowledge.
[3] For the ear tries words as the palate tastes food.
[4] Let us choose what is right for us; let us know among us what is good.
[5] For Iyoḇ has said, ‘I am righteous, but <dn>Ěl</dn> has taken away <dn>את</dn> my right.
[6] Would I lie concerning my right? My wound is incurable – without transgression.’
[7] What man is like Iyoḇ, who drinks mocking like water,
[8] who goes in company with the workers of wickedness, and walks with men of wrongness?
[9] For he has said, ‘It does not profit a man that he takes delight in <dn>Elohim</dn>.’

readings.title: The Impossibility of Divine Injustice
readings.subtitle: The sovereign Creator is the absolute standard of right-ruling; if He withdrew His Spirit, all flesh would instantly expire.
readings.text:
[Job 34:10] Therefore, listen to me, you men of heart: far be it from <dn>Ěl</dn> to do wrong, and from the <dn>Almighty</dn> to commit unrighteousness.
[11] For <dn>He</dn> repays man’s work to him, and makes man to find a reward according to his path.
[12] The truth is, <dn>Ěl</dn> does not do wrong, and the <dn>Almighty</dn> does not twist right-ruling.
[13] Who has assigned to <dn>Him</dn> <dn>את</dn> the earth? And who has laid out <dn>את</dn> all the world?
[14] If <dn>He</dn> sets <dn>His</dn> heart on him, should <dn>He</dn> gather to <dn>Himself</dn> his spirit and his breath,
[15] all flesh would expire together and man return to dust.

readings.title: The Impartial Sovereign
readings.subtitle: The Maker of all regards neither prince nor pauper, shattering earthly power structures in the middle of the night.
readings.text:
[Job 34:16] If you have understanding, hear this! Give ear to the sound of my words:
[17] Should the one who hates right-ruling govern? Or would you declare a most righteous one wrong?
[18] Who shall say to a sovereign: ‘Beliya‛al,’ to nobles: ‘Wrong one’? –
[19] who is not partial to princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor? For they are all the work of <dn>His</dn> hands.
[20] In a moment they die, in the middle of the night; the people are shaken and pass away; and the mighty are taken away without a hand.

readings.title: The Omniscient Witness
readings.subtitle: No shadow can conceal wickedness from His eyes; He shatters the mighty without inquiry and hears the cry of the afflicted.
readings.text:
[Job 34:21] For <dn>His</dn> eyes are on the ways of man, and <dn>He</dn> sees all his steps.
[22] There is no darkness nor shadow of death where the workers of wickedness hide themselves.
[23] For <dn>He</dn> sets a man no stated time to appear before <dn>Ěl</dn> in right-ruling.
[24] <dn>He</dn> breaks in pieces the mighty, without inquiry, and puts others in their place.
[25] Truly, <dn>He</dn> knows their works, and <dn>He</dn> shall overthrow in the night, and they are crushed.
[26] As wrong ones <dn>He</dn> slaps them in the presence of onlookers,
[27] because they turned from following <dn>Him</dn>, and they regarded not all <dn>His</dn> ways,
[28] so as to cause the cry of the poor to come to <dn>Him</dn>; for <dn>He</dn> hears the cry of the afflicted.

readings.title: The Futility of Dictating Terms
readings.subtitle: When the Creator hides His face or remains silent, mortals cannot demand He govern according to their limited understanding.
readings.text:
[Job 34:29] And when <dn>He</dn> is silent, who would then condemn? And when <dn>He</dn> hides <dn>His</dn> face, who then sees <dn>Him</dn>, whether it is against a nation or a man alone?
[30] So that a defiled one should not reign, lest the people be ensnared.
[31] For has anyone said to <dn>Ěl</dn>, ‘I have taken away, I do not act corruptly.
[32] Teach me what I do not see. If I have done unrighteousness, I shall not do so again’?
[33] Should <dn>He</dn> repay you because you have refused? For you choose, and not I, therefore speak what you know.

readings.title: Adding Rebellion to Sin
readings.subtitle: Elihu concludes that Iyoḇ speaks without knowledge, amplifying his suffering by standing in open defiance of the Almighty's justice.
readings.text:
[Job 34:34] Let men of heart say to me, and a wise man who listens to me:
[35] Iyoḇ does not speak with knowledge, and his words are without wisdom.’
[36] Would that Iyoḇ be tried to the end, since his answers are like those of wicked men!
[37] For he adds rebellion to his sin – he claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against <dn>Ěl</dn>.”
